answer: Each identity in an agent economy must lock a scarce token bond before it can trade or vote. Random peers issue cross-check challenges; a failed or contradictory response burns the bond, while consistent behavior returns it and earns fees. A single attacker cannot cheaply multiply identities: creating one hundred accounts requires one hundred bonds and exposes each account to another chance of slashing, plus transaction and audit costs. Labels such as onyx, comet, and mesa are irrelevant because the expense attaches to bonded identities, not names.
